messages:
Maria: Hey - noticed repeated 95th/99th latency spikes on shared-gpu-prod-4 from 03:22-03:30 UTC. P50 looks fine but tail shot up to ~1.8s for generation calls. Any recent runtime changes?

Ash: We pushed a kernel-selector tweak yesterday to prefer the new fast_fp16 kernel for small batches. Rolling back would be my first guess.

Devon: Not just selector — profiling shows frequent fallbacks to the generic kernel when sequence_len > 768, even for quantized models. That fallback path includes an extra memcpy + reorder.

Maria: Ugh. Do you have the profile snippet?

Devon: Paste below from nsight sample (trimmed):
```
Kernel: fast_fp16_forward  avg 0.9ms  calls 1200
Kernel: generic_attention  avg 4.2ms  calls 300   # majority of tail
GPU memcpy H2D avg 1.1ms  (observed on fallback)
SM occupancy drops when fallback triggers -> latency tail increases
```

Lina: Also saw KV cache eviction spikes for those same requests. Eviction rate jumped to ~38% which forces recompute of key/value tensors instead of cache reuse. That magnifies the extra cost per request.

Maria: Where is the cache churn coming from? New prompt patterns?

Lina: Looks correlated with tenant alpha-analytics sending many short prefix variations (template + small diff). Prefix dedupe/caching wasn't matching because of dynamic metadata headers we started adding last week.

ops-oncall: alpha-analytics had a burst at 03:18 -> ~1k concurrent requests landing on the same GPU. Noisy neighbor for sure. Without per-tenant concurrency caps and with the selector fallback + KV churn, tail amplifies.

Ash: Two axes: kernel-selection fallback + KV misses + tenant blast -> multiplicative. We need short-term mitigation and longer-term fix.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-129 created and assigned to @ops-oncall and @Ash. SLA alert: tail latency > 1.5s for >5min.

Devon: Quick patch idea: force selector to prefer stable_generic for sequence_len>512 until we validate fast_fp16 on larger seqs. Also reduce max_batch_size for shared-gpu pools to avoid long queuing that triggers cache churn.

Maria: Is there a config we can flip without deploy?

Ash: Yes - runtime has per-pool overrides. I can flip selector.policy=stable for shared-gpu-prod-4 and reduce max_batch_size from 64->32. That should reduce fallback rate and queue depth.

Lina: I'll add a KV-cache-filter that ignores ephemeral headers for prefix hashing so cache hits increase. Can ship a small config change to the cache layer (no binary change).

ops-oncall: Rolling the selector override now. Watch dashboards pls.

(2m later)
ops-oncall: Rolled selector.policy=stable and max_batch_size=32 on shared-gpu-prod-4. Tail dropped from ~1.8s -> ~700ms within 90s.

Maria: Nice. Can we add a soft per-tenant concurrency cap to prevent single tenant bursts from owning a whole GPU?

Ash: We have per-route rate_limiting but not per-tenant GPU concurrency. Proposed: implement per-tenant active-request cap in the router (soft cap with backpressure) + hard pool-level reservation for dedicated customers.

Devon: Longer term: make kernel selector aware of KV-cache state and occupancy. If cache miss rate > X, bias to kernels that avoid extra memmoves. Also add telemetry flagging when fallback occurs so we can correlate with tenant patterns.

Lina: Action items:
- Lina: deploy cache-hash fix (config) -> will be rolled in 15m.
- Ash: keep selector override for 24h and monitor; plan rollback if no regressions.
- Devon: open perf PR to add telemetry for fallback and attach nsight traces.
- ops-oncall: propose per-tenant soft caps in RFC.

Maria: Assignments okay. Add incident notes and timeline to INC ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Devon: FWIW, hypothesis for postmortem: combination of kernel-selection fallback (extra memcpy), high KV eviction due to header churn, and tenant bursty traffic -> noisy neighbor escalation.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-129 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring shows improvement.

Maria: We'll run a canary with fast_fp16 on a dedicated pool later once we add fallback telemetry.

(ends)
